title_en: Reply of the Supreme People's Court on Whether Industrial Unions and Grassroots Trade Unions Have the Status of Social Organizations as Legal Persons and Whether the Centralized Account for Trade Union Funds May Be Frozen or Transferred

articles.content_en: 2. The determination of the legal person status of an enterprise established by an industrial union or a grassroots union shall, in principle, be based on the business registration; the approval by its superior trade union pursuant to relevant provisions shall be a mandatory procedure, and the People's Court shall not freeze or transfer the funds of the superior trade union on this ground to repay the debts of the debtor enterprise. Where an enterprise with legal person status invested by an industrial union or a grassroots union has insufficient investment or withdraws capital, it shall make up the investment or assume liability within the scope of the false registered capital; if the investment is fully paid and there is no withdrawal of capital, when the enterprise is in debt, it shall assume limited liability with all its property or the property under its management and operation.

3. Pursuant to the provisions of the Trade Union Law, the trade union funds include membership dues paid by union members, the funds allocated by enterprises, institutions, and government organs that have established trade unions to the trade union at the rate of two percent of the total monthly wages of all employees, as well as the income turned over by enterprises and institutions under the trade union and subsidies from the people's government, etc. The trade union funds shall be allocated proportionally on a monthly basis to the local trade unions at all levels and the All-China Federation of Trade Unions. Once the trade union funds are allocated, the ownership thereof shall be transferred accordingly. The 'centralized account for trade union funds' opened independently in a bank has nothing to do with the enterprise's operating funds and is specifically used for the centralization and distribution of trade union funds. No expenses shall be disbursed from this account, nor shall funds be misappropriated or transferred. Therefore, when hearing a case, the People's Court shall not regard the trade union funds as the property of the enterprise in which the trade union is located, and when the enterprise is in debt, it shall not freeze or transfer the trade union funds and the money in the 'centralized account for trade union funds'.
Hereby reply.
May 16, 1997
